findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-040A Dom Care Contract Award (PART 1) - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Delegated authority to move providers between Tier 2 and Tier 1 creates price risk that must be absorbed within Adult Social Care departmental budget
findings.detail: The council grants delegated authority to the Director of Adult Social Care to move providers from Tier 2 (general framework) to Tier 1 (patch providers) via a reserve list mechanism. The paper identifies that unit prices may differ between tiers, and any cost increase from such movement must be managed within the director's existing budgetary envelope.
findings.matters: Identifies a discretionary spending risk within an already-committed departmental budget, requiring cost absorption if tier-movement decisions result in higher unit prices
findings.figures: None specified
findings.quote: There is some financial risk arising from the seeking of delegated authority to move providers from Tier 2 to Tier 1 as the unit price tendered might be different. If the price is higher, the risk shall be managed by the Director of Adult Social Care within their budgetary envelope.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-040A Dom Care Contract Award (PART 1) - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Framework contract contains no inflation until April 2028, then rises by CPI annually, providing two-year cost stability in a four-year commitment
findings.detail: The domiciliary care framework does not include contractual inflation adjustment until April 2028. From that point, prices will rise annually by CPI, currently assumed at government target of 2% per annum. This provides fixed costs for the initial two years of the four-year contract.
findings.matters: Provides cost stability in a large recurring service contract and aligns future inflation to government target-level CPI
findings.figures: No inflation until April 2028, thereafter 2% CPI assumed annually
findings.quote: There is some inflationary risk mitigation in that there is no contractual inflation to be applied until April 2028.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-040A Dom Care Contract Award (PART 1) - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Council confirms adequate budgetary provision for £20.3m annual domiciliary care contract while identifying demand-led service risks to be managed within departmental budgets
findings.detail: The council states there is adequate budgetary provision across Adult Services (£18.8m) and Children's Services (£1.5m) for the new framework. However, it explicitly identifies that risks from demand-led spending will be managed by respective directors to ensure their departmental budgets outturn within the agreed envelope.
findings.matters: Shows council's governance mechanism for managing volatility and cost exposure in a major recurring demand-led service budget
findings.figures: £18.8m Adult Social Care budget, £1.5m Children's Social Care budget, total £20.3m annual
findings.quote: There are risks to the budget arising from it being a demand led service. Such risks shall be managed by the respective Directors to ensure that their departmental budgets as a whole outturn within the budgetary envelope.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-037 Appendix A - Transformation and Improvement - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: £906,000 of £1.830m recurring savings target delivered as of July 2026, with March 2027 deadline
findings.detail: The Adult Services Transformation and Improvement Programme reports £906,000 of recurring savings delivered by July 2026 against a target of £1.830m by March 2027. Identified contributions include £631,000 from optimised care and support packages and £268,000 from the front door redesign. The programme reports green status across most constituent projects and is described as 'on track' and 'progressing as planned'.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders track delivery against committed savings targets in Medium Term Financial Plans; shortfalls require budget adjustment or reserve drawdown, while delivery on track confirms programme discipline and the council's ability to execute its financial plan.
findings.figures: £906,000 delivered as of July 2026; £1.830m target by March 2027; £631,000 from optimised care and support packages; £268,000 from front door redesign
findings.quote: As of July 2026, the Programme has delivered £906,000 of recurring savings against a target of £1.830m by March 2027

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-037 Adult Services Transformation and Improvement Update Report - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Programme in year three; Strategic Delivery Partner contract with Social Care Institute for Excellence concluded
findings.detail: The council is four months into the third year of the programme, described as firmly established and delivering significant service improvements. The SCIE contract for external delivery support has concluded, with the programme having embedded the approaches, tools, and capabilities developed during the partnership.
findings.matters: Transition from external expert support to internal delivery is a sustainability checkpoint; if capabilities have not been properly embedded, the council faces risk to programme delivery and unanticipated costs for alternative support
findings.figures: Year 3 of programme; SCIE contract concluded
findings.quote: The Strategic Delivery Partner contract with the Social Care Institute for Excellence (SCIE), which provided expert supported to Adult Service's Transformation and Improvement Programme during the previous year, has now concluded.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-037 Adult Services Transformation and Improvement Update Report - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: First two years of transformation programme fully funded through £2m Disabled Facilities Grant and £1.6m carried-forward iBCF balance
findings.detail: Executive approved in July 2024 the use of £2m of DFG and £1.6m of improved Better Care Fund carry-forward to fully fund the investment phase. This covers programme costs through to 2026/27, when savings materialise.
findings.matters: Identifying non-revenue funding sources for the investment phase is critical to the credibility of any savings plan; without funding cover, the council would need to find revenue budget or incur debt during years 1–2
findings.figures: £2m DFG (in principle); £1.6m iBCF carry-forward
findings.quote: Executive agreed the use, in principle, of £2m of DFG and £1.6m of iBCF, which would fully fund the costs of the first 2 years of the Adult Services Digital Transformation Programme 'Invest to Save' proposal

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-037 Adult Services Transformation and Improvement Update Report - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Adult Services Transformation programme projected to deliver £1.9m p.a. net savings from 2027/28 on a £10.9m five-year investment
findings.detail: The programme will result in net costs of £876k in 2024/25 and £674k in 2025/26, then net savings of £1,730k, £1,900k, and £1,914k for 2026/27–2028/29 respectively, with the £1.9m p.a. figure recurring for future years beyond 2028/29. The council states this programme will help reduce its forecast budget gap from 2026/27 onwards.
findings.matters: This is part of Bromley's financial strategy to manage demand and cost pressures in adult social care; lenders track whether councils' transformation programmes deliver planned savings on schedule
findings.figures: £10.9m gross cost over 5 years; net costs £876k (2024/25), £674k (2025/26); net savings £1,730k (2026/27), £1,900k (2027/28), £1,914k (2028/29); £1.9m p.a. recurring from 2027/28 onwards
findings.quote: net savings of £1.9m p.a. from 2027/28

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: FSD26043 Budget Monitoring Q1 2026-27 - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Delivery of significant in-year savings targets is critical to controlling budget position and currently at risk from service capacity constraints
findings.detail: The department has significant savings targets to deliver alongside business as usual in 2026-27. The Director reports oversight is robust and savings are currently on track, but acknowledges dependency on available capacity within the service and the challenge of financial modelling reflecting actual delivery impact. Underperformance would worsen the budget position during the year.
findings.matters: The reported overspend is manageable in part because savings delivery is assumed. If savings do not materialise, the full-year effect will worsen. Savings at risk from capacity constraints is an operational risk that affects the financial outcome.
findings.figures: No quantum given
findings.quote: The department has significant savings targets to achieve in year alongside business as usual. Under-delivery of any of those savings will see a worsened position as we move through the year. Oversight of progress towards achieving savings is robust and currently on track to deliver, but actions are dependent on capacity within the service

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: FSD26043 Budget Monitoring Q1 2026-27 - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Adult social care at risk from demand volatility, care provider price pressures, and provider sustainability concerns
findings.detail: The Director identifies demand-led service pressures (unexpected large care packages, potential new liabilities for ordinarily resident residents) and external market pressures (care price increases) as risks to in-year spend. Additional risk flagged: provider failure due to financial unsustainability and potential handback of care packages to other boroughs. The service manages over 3,500 residents, making volatility material.
findings.matters: These risks could cause material deterioration in the reported position during the year. Provider failure or package handback would require rapid replacement care provision at potentially higher cost, worsening the overspend. Price and demand volatility in a £132m budget is material to outturn risk.
findings.figures: Over 3,500 residents at any one time
findings.quote: There remains a risk of increased overspend in year due to the demand led nature of the service, pressure on the price of care that has to be purchased in year from external providers and the potential for unexpected large new packages of care

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: FSD26043 Budget Monitoring Q1 2026-27 - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Adult social care budget alignment improved against 2025-26 following tighter budget setting and spending controls
findings.detail: The Director of Adult Social Care credits the better Q1 position to more accurate budget setting in 2026-27, improved monitoring, stronger spend controls, and delivery of significant savings within the department. This is presented as an improvement on the prior year, suggesting that previous forecasting issues have been addressed.
findings.matters: Improved budget discipline and forecasting accuracy across a £132m service is material evidence of management capability; it also suggests the overspend, though real, occurs within a framework of better control than the prior year.
findings.figures: Comparison implicit; portfolio budget £132.066m
findings.quote: This first budget monitoring report for 2026/27 shows closer alignment with the budget set and the spend in Adult services than was seen last year. This is as a result more accurate budget setting, monitoring, strong spend controls and delivery of significant savings within the department.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: FSD26043 Budget Monitoring Q1 2026-27 - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Adult Care and Health Portfolio projects £642k overspend in Q1 2026-27 with full year effect of £1,137k
findings.detail: The portfolio is showing a £642k overspend position based on June 2026 expenditure data. Assessment & Care Management is the largest pressure at £1,308k overspend, followed by Mental Health at £828k overspend. These are substantially offset by a Learning Disabilities underspend of £1,277k. The paper notes this position represents closer alignment with budget than was achieved in 2025-26.
findings.matters: An in-year overspend with material full-year effect signals whether the council's overall budget strategy is tracking. The offset by a large underspend in Learning Disabilities indicates the overspend is not evenly distributed, which may matter for next year's budget design.
findings.figures: £642k overspend (full year effect £1,137k); Assessment & Care Management £1,308k overspend; Mental Health £828k overspend; Learning Disabilities £1,277k underspend
findings.quote: Overall, a £642k overspend position (full year effect of £1,137k) is projected, based on the information available in the first quarter of the 2026/27 financial year

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Council repurposing £9m DfE allocation to satellite units strategy, targeting 152 new SEND places to reduce out-of-borough placements and transport costs
findings.detail: Shortage of local specialist SEND provision drives high numbers of out-of-borough and independent provider placements, with independent schools costing £10-30k per pupil (double LA provision). Council increasing local capacity through satellite units within mainstream schools with 152 new placements planned (100 available January 2027, 52 in phase 2), using £9m DfE allocation originally proposed for free school. Strategy aims to reduce reliance on expensive independent provision and lower SEN transport costs, which report identifies as continuing risk area.
findings.matters: This capital-to-operations solution addresses both placement costs (independent provision premium) and transport costs. The fact DfE allocation has been flexed to support strategy suggests government agreement. Cost benefit depends on uptake and redirection of existing demand away from independent provision.
findings.figures: 152 new SEND places (100 by January 2027, 52 phase 2); £9m DfE allocation; independent provision £10-30k per pupil vs LA provision; SEN Transport identified as continuing risk area
findings.quote: The £9m from the DfE in place of the originally proposed free school will be used to secure these 152 new places without further delay.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: 2026/27 cost pressures will have £1,058k unmitigated full-year impact on 2027/28 budget unless further action taken
findings.detail: The overspend cost pressures identified in 2026/27 monitoring (primarily EHCP growth, placement costs, staffing) will have unmitigated full-year impact of £1,058k flowing into 2027/28. Management action is assumed within this projection, but report emphasizes further action will be needed to prevent impact on subsequent years. Report notes strict budgetary control is imperative given council faces significant financial savings requirements over next four years.
findings.matters: This shows the structural rather than one-off nature of cost pressures. If underlying drivers (EHCP growth, placement market costs, staffing challenges) are not resolved, the overspend will compound year-on-year.
findings.figures: £1,058k unmitigated full-year impact into 2027/28; assumes management action is taken
findings.quote: The cost pressures identified in section 4 above will impact in 2027/28 by £1,058k.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Children's Social Care carrying £1m additional staffing costs while permanency recruitment improves to 94%
findings.detail: CSC overspend includes £1m in additional staffing costs from interims and agency staff, cover for maternity and long-term sickness, and continuing temporary staffing beyond budgeted terms. Permanency levels now at 94% including 'in pipeline' appointments, with new Deputy HR permanent member appointed to focus on CEF. Recruitment remains challenging nationally across social work profession.
findings.matters: Staffing costs drive a significant portion of the CSC overspend, reflecting national market pressures (shortage of qualified social workers) and local recruitment challenges. The council's improvement to 94% permanency suggests progress, but agency cost pressures remain immediate.
findings.figures: £1m additional staffing costs in CSC; 94% permanency levels including 'in pipeline' appointments
findings.quote: The continued progress in recruiting permanent staff (94%), reducing reliance on agency staff, and the ASYE programme have reduced spend but some agency staff still contribute to an overspend awaiting HR processes.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Children, Education and Families portfolio forecasts £1,782k controllable overspend with targeted mitigating actions delivering partial relief
findings.detail: Controllable overspend stands at £1,782k as at end-June 2026 (1.6% of £108.4m budget), with Education overspending by £660k and Children's Social Care by £1,122k. However, specific mitigating actions are delivering results: Solace Rise new children's home completed with children transitioning from expensive out-of-borough placements; 29 young people successfully moved into housing with estimated £400k savings; block bed provision achieving 100% occupancy (predicted 80%), reducing cost of expensive placements.
findings.matters: The scale of overspend shows material cost pressures that exceed budget assumptions. The council is demonstrating it can deploy targeted solutions that deliver savings. For a finance director, the key question is whether these specific interventions can offset structural demand pressures if EHCP growth and placement costs continue.
findings.figures: £1,782k controllable overspend; £108.379m total portfolio budget; Education £660k overspend; CSC £1,122k overspend; £400k estimated savings from housing moves; 100% occupancy vs 80% predicted on block beds
findings.quote: The latest projected overspend of £1,782,000 is forecast on the controllable budget, based on information as at June 2026

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: EHCP numbers reached 4,982 at end-June 2026, up 9% year-on-year and running 45 above estimated target for 2026/27
findings.detail: EHCP rolls at end June 2026 stood at 4,982, up 427 (9%) from 4,555 a year earlier, running 45 above estimated target for 2026/27 and requiring additional spend not budgeted. Service predicted annual increase of 344 but national picture shows 415% increase in EHCP numbers since Children and Families Act, with tribunal challenges up 43%. Bromley has implemented new guidance on Ordinarily Available Provision and statutory assessment thresholds to manage demand, but year-on-year growth continues at around 10%.
findings.matters: EHCP demand growth is structural and outpacing budget assumptions. It drives both the £17.6m DSG overspend and unsustainable pressure on placement capacity and transport costs. A peer council would need to understand whether Bromley's demand management efforts are effective or whether this is an unavoidable national trend.
findings.figures: 4,982 EHCPs at end June 2026, up 427 from 4,555 (9% growth); currently 45 over target; predicted annual increase 344; national increase 415% since Children and Families Act; tribunal challenges up 43% nationally
findings.quote: The current number of EHCP's as at the end of June 2026 is 4,982, up 427 from 4,555 at the end of June 2025, an increase of around 9%.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: 90% of Bromley's historic SEND deficit to be written off under government reform, subject to High Needs Stability Grant confirmation
findings.detail: Government announced February 2026 that 90% of councils' historic DSG deficits (accrued to end 2025/26) will be written off through a new national grant, reducing Bromley's £35,981k accumulated deficit to £3,998k responsibility. Bromley submitted local SEND reform plan in June 2026; formal confirmation expected mid-September 2026, with draw-down in November 2026.
findings.matters: This transforms Bromley's financial position by removing £35.9m of accumulated deficit liability, if confirmed. A finance director or peer council would need to understand whether they will receive equivalent relief and how to manage finances during the interim period.
findings.figures: £35,981k historic DSG deficit → £3,998k remaining responsibility; £17,584k in-year DSG overspend 2026/27; confirmation deadline mid-September 2026; draw-down November 2026
findings.quote: In February 2026, the government announced that 90% of Councils historic SEND deficits (accrued up to the end of 2025/26) will be written off, funded by a new national grant.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: High Needs Stability Grant funding from DfE expected autumn 2026 but guaranteed no later than March 2027
findings.detail: The document notes that once DfE approval is given, High Needs Stability Grant funding is expected to be released by autumn 2026, with March 2027 as the latest guaranteed date. This funding is critical to stabilising the high needs system during the transition period while the reform programme takes effect.
findings.matters: Establishes the timeline for receipt of the conditional funding that underpins the council's financial position; March 2027 deadline defines when the council must have confirmed this funding source.
findings.figures: Autumn 2026 expected; March 2027 latest deadline
findings.quote: once approval is given, High Needs Stability Grant funding is expected to be released by autumn, but by March 2027 at the latest.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: £2.664,902 DfE grant allocation for 2026/27 Experts at Hand programme, with further allocations expected 2027/28 and 2028/29
findings.detail: In 2026/27, the Experts at Hand allocation is £2,664,902, structured to the DfE's 80/10/10 model with more than 80% focused on direct frontline delivery, less than 10% on transformation, and less than 10% on administration. Further grant allocations are expected in 2027/28 and 2028/29, though amounts are not specified in the paper.
findings.matters: Details the phased external funding for reform delivery; the council will need to fund programme continuation from 2030 onwards or secure extended grant funding to sustain the model beyond the current allocation cycle.
findings.figures: £2,664,902 (2026/27); 80% frontline, less than 10% transformation, less than 10% administration
findings.quote: In 2026/27, the Experts at Hand allocation is £2,664,902. This is aligned to the expected 80/10/10 model, with more than 80% focused on direct frontline delivery, less than 10% on transformation, and less than 10% on administration and programme management.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Workforce capacity and recruitment constraints rated Red risk, threatening delivery of projected £12.52m savings
findings.detail: The plan identifies workforce capacity and recruitment constraints as its single Red-rated delivery risk. It proposes recruiting up to 17 additional posts from Experts at Hand grant funding and expanding speech and language therapy to 40 FTE, occupational therapy to 19.2 FTE and educational psychology to 24.79 FTE by 2028/29. The council acknowledges that recruitment and retention remain significant risks given national competition for specialist roles.
findings.matters: The highest-rated delivery risk directly threatens the financial projections on which the council's plan depends; failure to recruit specialist capacity would delay or prevent realisation of projected cost reductions.
findings.figures: Up to 17 additional posts from grant; SaLT to 40 FTE; OT to 19.2 FTE; EP to 24.79 FTE by 2028/29
findings.quote: Recruitment and retention remain significant risks, particularly given national competition for specialist roles.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Plan projects £12.52m High Needs budget cost reduction and £1.67m SEN Transport saving by 2029/30, conditional on delivery of multi-year reform programme
findings.detail: The reform programme aims to achieve financial sustainability through reducing escalation to high-cost placements via earlier intervention, increased mainstream inclusion and local sufficiency. The financial impact is phased, with continued demand growth expected in early years and material cost reductions only from 2028 onwards as workforce capacity and inclusion practice take effect, explicitly dependent on successful delivery of the Experts at Hand model, workforce expansion, and sustained partner commitment.
findings.matters: Finance directors need visibility of both savings targets and the critical path dependencies that must be met; timing shows only modest financial impact before 2028 with material savings heavily dependent on multi-partner reform delivery over three years.
findings.figures: £12.52m High Needs cost reduction; £1.67m SEN Transport saving; both by 2029/30; inflection point from 2028 onwards
findings.quote: The Plan anticipates that the reform programme will contribute to a £12.52m High Needs budget cost reduction by 2029/30, alongside a £1.67m reduction in SEN Transport expenditure by 2029/30. These projections are dependent on successful delivery of the Experts at Hand model, workforce expansion, local sufficiency and inclusion base development, and continued partner commitment to earlier intervention and shared accountability.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Annex A - The Local SEND Reform Plan
findings.headline: Workforce capacity and recruitment constraints rated as Critical/Likely risk to plan delivery, with national shortages and local competition limiting specialist staff supply
findings.detail: The partnership has identified workforce capacity as a Critical-rated risk with Likely likelihood, threatening the ability to recruit and retain sufficient specialist and support staff at scale across speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, educational psychology and specialist teaching. Mitigations include joint commissioning between LA and ICB and exploration of reciprocal arrangements with other areas, but supply-side constraints are noted as systemic.
findings.matters: Workforce cost inflation and recruitment difficulty are live pressures in many councils' SEND systems; a plan-critical risk rated Critical/Likely suggests the savings pathway is contingent on outcomes outside the council's direct control, materially affecting delivery probability.
findings.figures: Critical/Likely RAG rating; national workforce shortages explicitly cited as constraint
findings.quote: Risk that national workforce shortages and local competition limit the ability to recruit and retain sufficient specialist and support staff to deliver the reform programme at scale.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Annex A - The Local SEND Reform Plan
findings.headline: £2.66m Experts at Hand investment in year 1 (2026/27), with >80% (£2.13m) deployed to frontline clinical and specialist staff delivery
findings.detail: The plan directs £2,664,902 to launch the Experts at Hand early intervention model in its first year, with majority funding (>£2.1m) allocated to frontline workforce including specialist teachers, speech and language therapists, occupational therapists and educational psychologists. Remaining <10% each for transformation activity and programme administration. This represents material new recurrent investment to drive the projected savings.
findings.matters: The funding model and allocation show whether the council is investing adequately to achieve stated savings, and whether transformation is properly resourced; underinvestment in frontline delivery would undermine the entire savings plan's credibility.
findings.figures: Total EAH allocation £2,664,902; direct delivery £2,132,433 (>80%); transformation £266,490 (<10%); administration £265,979 (<10%)
findings.quote: Total EAH allocation Total funding allocated to the Experts at Hand model £ 2,664,902 100% Direct delivery Frontline workforce including Specialist Teachers, SaLT, OT, EP and associated delivery staff £2,132,433 >80%

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Annex A - The Local SEND Reform Plan
findings.headline: EHCP caseload growth projected to moderate from 4,784 (2025) to 5,633 by 2029, with growth rate slowing from 2028
findings.detail: Current demand for statutory assessment remains high at 1,065 EHC needs assessment requests and 756 plans issued annually. The plan projects total EHCP growth of 849 over four years (17.7%), but projects the rate to decelerate from 2028, suggesting earlier intervention is expected to suppress future demand growth. Demand management is central to the £14.19m savings pathway.
findings.matters: Demand trajectory directly drives high needs expenditure and determines whether cost reductions are sustainable; a council successfully moderating demand growth demonstrates system-level reform traction, whereas acceleration would signal reform plan failure.
findings.figures: 4,784 EHCPs (December 2025); 5,633 projected by 2029; 1,065 annual assessment requests; 756 plans issued annually
findings.quote: Demand for SEND support has grown significantly, with 4,784 children and young people with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) in 2025, placing sustained pressure on mainstream inclusion, specialist sufficiency, workforce capacity and the financial sustainability of the high needs system.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Annex A - The Local SEND Reform Plan
findings.headline: 435 pupils placed in expensive independent and non-maintained specialist settings, creating sustained high-cost pressure that plan aims to reduce from 2028
findings.detail: Bromley has higher proportion of independent placements (7% of EHCP cohort) than national and London averages (5%), with over 400 children placed in these settings often outside the borough. This drives material cost pressure on the high needs block and generates additional transport costs. The reform strategy focuses on expanding local provision to reduce reliance on these placements from 2028 onwards.
findings.matters: Independent placements are high-unit-cost drivers of high needs pressure; the scale of this cohort (435 pupils) and the plan's timeline for reduction are directly material to understanding whether the council's cost pressures are being actively managed or are structural.
findings.figures: 435 children and young people placed in NMSS or independent provision; 7% of EHCP cohort vs 5% national/London average; over 400 out-of-borough placements
findings.quote: Over 400 children are placed in these settings, often outside the borough, increasing transport and placement costs. Our strategy focuses on expanding local provision, particularly for SLCN, ASD, SEMH, and complex needs.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Annex A - The Local SEND Reform Plan
findings.headline: Partnership targets £12.52m reduction in high needs spending by 2029/30, with additional £1.67m savings in SEN transport
findings.detail: The reform plan projects total cost reductions of £14.19m by 2029/30 through moderated EHCP growth, reduced independent placement reliance, and expanded local capacity. The timeline extends to 2029/30 with growth expected to slow from 2028 onwards. Success is contingent on delivering the Experts at Hand early intervention model and expanding local specialist provision.
findings.matters: High needs deficits are a material pressure for many councils; a savings plan of this scale with a specific timeline and CFO sign-off is directly relevant to peers assessing fiscal sustainability and to lenders evaluating medium-term budget risk.
findings.figures: £12.52m high needs cost reduction by 2029/30; £1.67m SEN transport reduction by 2029/30; total £14.19m target
findings.quote: The partnership anticipates a total High Needs budget cost reduction of £12.52m by 2029/30 (see Data table 1 and Assumptions) and a £1.67m reduced expenditure on SEN Transport by 2029/30

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: School place planning adjusted to deliver SEN provision through satellite sites in existing schools rather than new special school.
findings.detail: The council is delivering 152 SEN places through satellite sites in existing schools rather than building the planned Redwood Academy special school. The first provision is scheduled to open in 2027. This represents an adaptation in capital strategy to meet statutory place sufficiency requirements.
findings.matters: Capital scheme changes affect council spending plans and debt requirements; a shift from new build to satellite sites typically reduces capital cost and ongoing revenue commitments.
findings.figures: 152 SEN places; first satellite site opening 2027.
findings.quote: Deliver 152 places that would have been provided through Redwood Academy SEN special school through the delivery of SEN satellite sites of existing schools. First provision to open by 2027.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: NHS restructuring creates risk of unfunded service transfer if areas shift to public health without budget.
findings.detail: The restructuring of NHS England includes 50% cuts to Integrated Care Boards and cuts to UKHSA. The council notes that some safeguarding and infection control functions may be cut, and some areas may shift to public health without accompanying budget. The council is engaged to understand implications and retain key staff.
findings.matters: Unfunded service transfers increase council cost pressures; a 50% ICB cut and potential service shift without funding is material downside risk for social care and public health funding.
findings.figures: 50% cuts to Integrated Care Board; cuts to UKHSA; potential unfunded service shift.
findings.quote: Possible consequential shift of some areas to public health without the budget

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: SEND transport transformation successfully reduced vehicle numbers and daily costs through tendering.
findings.detail: The council implemented transformation options approved by Portfolio Holder and Executive to reduce demand for travel assistance through revised policy and independent travel training. A tendering exercise based on optimised routes successfully reduced the number of vehicles operating and average daily costs. Work is underway to procure a new framework contract commencing September 2027.
findings.matters: SEND transport is a high-cost demand-led service; successful cost management demonstrates the council's ability to control spending pressures through service transformation.
findings.figures: Vehicle numbers reduced; average daily costs reduced; framework contract commencing September 2027.
findings.quote: The tendering exercise based on the optimised routes has been successfully delivered reducing the numbers of vehicles operating and reducing the average daily costs of routes.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: DSG Deficit Recovery Plan agreed and being considered for 2025/26 MTFS.
findings.detail: The council has agreed principles for a Dedicated Schools Grant Deficit Recovery Plan with SEND Governance Board and Schools Forum, with the detailed plan being considered for the 2025/26 Medium Term Financial Strategy. This addresses structural underfunding affecting education and high-needs services, where 80% of Children's Services operations are demand-led and subject to cost volatility from complex placements and rising demand.
findings.matters: DSG deficits are a material pressure for councils nationally; the council's recovery plan is a critical tool for managing medium-term financial sustainability.
findings.figures: 80% of Children's Services operations are demand-led; gross risk rated 5×5=25, current 4×5=20.
findings.quote: DSG Deficit Recovery Plan principles agreed by SEND Governance Board and Schools Forum. Detailed Plan being considered as part of 2025/26 MTFS.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: CEF Digital Transformation Programme reported slightly delayed but on track to complete within current financial year
findings.detail: The first part of the digital children's programme has gone live; discovery stage and proposed solutions identified. The programme is slightly delayed from original plan but expected to complete by end of 2026/27. Budget reduced from £121k to £115k.
findings.matters: Digital transformation delay is a relatively minor slip but indicates some project delivery challenges; completion is still forecast within the year.
findings.figures: Budget reduced from £121k to £115k; £0k actual spend in Q1
findings.quote: The Programme is slightly delayed but will be completed by the end of 26/26

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: New Childcare Places Grant projects delayed pending planning permission; no further applications planned
findings.detail: Three childcare places projects are awaiting planning permission and have been re-profiled from £373k to £218k in 2026/27. The commentary notes there are no plans in place for another round of applications, indicating a halt in pipeline development for this scheme.
findings.matters: Stalled project pipeline with no forward strategy for replacement bids suggests childcare places expansion programme may not be progressing as anticipated.
findings.figures: Budget estimate fell from £373k to £218k in 2026/27
findings.quote: Awaiting planning permission for 3 other projects. There are no plans in place for another round applications.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Significant £6.7m rephasing out of current year reflects revised delivery timescales across multiple schemes
findings.detail: As part of Q1 monitoring, £7.556m has been moved from 2026/27 and 2028/29 into future financial years to reflect revised estimates of delivery timing. The net effect is £6.721m out of 2026/27, distributed across 2027/28 (£3.482m), 2029/30 (£4.074m), and other years. Current year budget fell from £19.5m (pre-Q1) to £12.9m (post-Q1).
findings.matters: Rephasing indicates slippage in project delivery timescales; councils and lenders monitor spend profiles to assess delivery risk and whether schemes are on track.
findings.figures: £7,556k rephased; £6,721k net from 2026/27; 2026/27 budget reduced from £19,540k to £12,855k
findings.quote: A total of £7,556k has been re-phased from 2026/27 and 2028/29 into future financial years to reflect revised estimates of when expenditure is likely to be incurred.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: £6.8m in additional Basic Need education capital funding granted and added to the revised programme for 2030/31
findings.detail: The council has received supplementary capital funding in support of its Education Capital Programme. This new grant funding of £6.852m for Basic Need (school places) is being added to the capital programme and pushed into 2030/31. Combined with £39k Devolved Formula Capital added in Q1, the total new funding approved is £6.891k.
findings.matters: New funding awarded is a positive indicator of the council's financial position and education infrastructure priorities; it increases total available resources for the CEF portfolio from £54.8m to £61.7m.
findings.figures: Basic Need grant £6,852k; Devolved Formula Capital £39k; total new funding £6,891k
findings.quote: Subject to Executive approval, additional grant of £6,852k is requested to be incorporated into the existing capital scheme. This fund represents supplementary capital funding awarded to the Council in support of its Education Capital Programme.

findings.committee: Children, Education and Families Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Planning delays pushing back construction on multiple Operational Property Review schemes in the current year
findings.detail: Castlecombe Children's Centre, Blenheim Centre, and Adult Education schemes are all affected by planning delays that have deferred tender and construction work. The delays are pushing schemes out of the current financial year, contributing to a £6.7m rephasing out of 2026/27 to future years. OPR schemes as a whole were budgeted at £4.4m but are now estimated at £4.1m in 2026/27.
findings.matters: Planning delays create delivery risk and timing uncertainty; councils and lenders need visibility of whether capital projects will deliver as planned or slip into future years.
findings.figures: OPR schemes budget £4,408k Feb 2026 vs £4,082k Q1 estimate; £6,721k rephased from 2026/27 to future years
findings.quote: Delays in planning process for Castlecombe have pushed the construction programme out. Similarly delays with planning and design works for Blenheim have delayed the tender and subsequent works on site.

news_drafts.lead: Identifies a discretionary spending risk within an already-committed departmental budget, requiring cost absorption if tier-movement decisions result in higher unit prices
